## Market context

### Adoption has grown for three years but the gap to peers is widening

::::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width="55%"}

```{r}
#| label: chart-adoption
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.2

adoption <- tibble(
  year  = rep(2021:2025, 2),
  group = rep(c("Nexer clients", "Sector average"), each = 5),
  value = c(12, 19, 28, 41, 58, 15, 24, 38, 57, 82)
)

ggplot(adoption, aes(year, value, colour = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.4) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "Nexer clients"   = nexer_colours[["purple"]],
    "Sector average"  = nexer_colours[["grey"]]
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Adoption index",
    subtitle = paste(
      nexer_span("Nexer clients", nexer_colours[["purple"]]),
      "vs",
      nexer_span("sector average", nexer_colours[["grey"]])
    )
  ) +
  theme_nexer()
```

::: {.units}
Index, 2021 = 12
:::

::::

:::: {.column width="45%"}

#### Key drivers

- Tooling became cheap enough to trial without a business case
- Procurement cycles shortened from nine months to about six weeks
- Internal champions replaced central mandates

::: {.takeaway}
The gap is a **distribution** problem, not a capability one.
:::

## Options

### Three routes are open, and they differ mainly in who carries the risk

| Route | What it involves | Risk sits with | Time to value |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pilot first** | One team, one workflow, fixed scope | Nexer | ~6 weeks |
| **Platform first** | Build shared tooling, then onboard teams | Shared | ~6 months |
| **Buy and adapt** | Licence a vendor product, configure it | Client | ~3 months |

::: {.source}
[Note:]{.label} Time to value measured from contract signature to first production use.
:::

::: {.notes}
Options tables are for decisions, not inventories. Three rows, one differentiating
column — here it is who carries the risk. If every column differs, you have not
found the real trade-off yet.
:::

## Bridge

### Two thirds of the saving comes from a single lever

```{r}
#| label: chart-bridge
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.4

bridge <- tibble(
  step  = c("Baseline", "Process\nautomation", "Vendor\nconsolidation",
            "Rework\nreduction", "Target"),
  value = c(120, -52, -14, -12, 42),
  kind  = c("total", "delta", "delta", "delta", "total")
) |>
  mutate(
    idx   = row_number(),
    end   = c(120, 68, 54, 42, 42),
    start = c(0, 120, 68, 54, 0)
  )

ggplot(bridge, aes(x = reorder(step, idx))) +
  geom_rect(
    aes(xmin = idx - 0.38, xmax = idx + 0.38,
        ymin = pmin(start, end), ymax = pmax(start, end), fill = kind)
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = idx, y = pmax(start, end) + 5,
        label = ifelse(kind == "total", value, paste0(value))),
    family = nexer_font_body(), size = 5.2, colour = "#4a4a4a"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    total = nexer_colours[["purple"]],
    delta = nexer_colours[["orange"]]
  )) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = bridge$step) +
  labs(
    title = "Cost bridge, baseline to target",
    subtitle = paste(
      nexer_span("Position", nexer_colours[["purple"]]), "and",
      nexer_span("movement", nexer_colours[["orange"]])
    )
  ) +
  theme_nexer()
```

::: {.units}
€ millions, annualised
:::

::: {.source}
[Note:]{.label} Figures rounded to the nearest million; totals may not sum. &nbsp; [Source:]{.label} Engagement model v4
:::

::: {.notes}
A bridge answers "where does the number come from". Label the start bar, the end
bar, and every step between — an unlabelled segment is an invitation to be asked
about it.
:::

## Recommendation

### Start with one workflow, prove it in six weeks, then decide on the platform

::: {.incremental}

- **Weeks 1–2** — pick the workflow with the clearest baseline and the least integration
- **Weeks 3–5** — build in the open, with the receiving team in the room
- **Week 6** — measure against the baseline; publish the result either way

:::

::: {.takeaway}
The decision this deck asks for is the **six-week pilot**, not the platform.
:::
